title: Two Pointers and Sliding Window Check
description: Predict pointer movement and complexity for two-pointer and sliding-window patterns.

questions.prompt: In the two-pointer `twoSum` on a sorted array, if `sortedArr[left] + sortedArr[right] < target`, what should happen next?

options.text: Move `left` one step right (increase the sum)
Move `right` one step left (decrease the sum)
Move both pointers to the middle
Restart from the beginning

questions.explanation: If the sum is too small, you need a bigger value; moving `left` right on a sorted array increases the sum.

questions.prompt: Why does the sorted two-pointer approach run in `O(n)` instead of `O(n^2)`?

options.text: Because it uses recursion instead of loops
Because each pointer moves at most `n` times total, instead of re-checking every pair
Because it sorts the array first, which is free
Because JavaScript arrays are hash maps internally

questions.explanation: Each pointer only moves forward (or backward) and never revisits a position, bounding total pointer movement to `O(n)` instead of checking all `n^2` pairs.

questions.prompt: In the sliding window for longest unique substring, when do you shrink the window from the left?

options.text: Every single iteration, regardless of content
When the character at `right` is already in the current window
Only when the window reaches the end of the string
Never — the window only grows

questions.explanation: The window shrinks from the left only when a duplicate character is found, removing characters until the duplicate is gone.

questions.prompt: Why is it safe to shrink the sliding window from the left without missing a better answer?

options.text: Because the window is always sorted
Because any smaller window contained in the current one was already considered as `best` was updated
Because JavaScript strings are immutable
It is not safe — this is a bug in the pattern

questions.explanation: As `right` advances, `best` is updated on every valid window, so shrinking from the left never discards an answer better than what has already been recorded.

questions.prompt: Two pointers moving from each end toward the middle is most directly applicable when the array is:

options.text: Unsorted and contains duplicates
Sorted, so comparing the sum to the target tells you which pointer to move
A linked list, not an array
Guaranteed to have no valid answer

questions.explanation: The sorted order is what makes the pointer decision (move left vs. move right) correct — without it, moving a pointer could skip the answer.

questions.prompt: What is the overall time complexity of the sliding window `longestUnique` function?

options.text: `O(n^2)`, because of the inner `while`
`O(n)`, because `left` and `right` together make at most `2n` moves
`O(log n)`

questions.explanation: Even though there's a nested `while`, `left` can only advance up to `n` times total across the whole run, so the combined work is still `O(n)`.
